title: 3D fighting game
author: Wild-Elevator6639
selftext:
I want to create a Muay Thai fighting game, similar to EA UFC or Tekken. My plan was to have use Meshy/Tripo, Astra, Blender and Unity.

Is something like this possible with AI? I really want to emphasize good technique and realism but it seems like the animations--especially things like clinch--might be difficult to replicate. 

How would you go about doing something like this?

comments.author: Vumsy101
comments.body: You need to decide first which you're going for first. 3D Fighting game as a genre is Tekken. Strict frame by frame rules and deterministic. UFC is a Sports game, and is more loose and physics driven in comparison. They're really not the same.

replies.author: Wild-Elevator6639
replies.body: Definitely more of the sports game route. I used Tekken as an example to emphasize that it's not a 2d game and should allow for lateral motion

replies.author: Vumsy101
replies.body:
You'll likely need a dedicated posing AI and feed a lot of reference images + some poses of your own.

When I rawdogged testing 3D animations with Astra, my experience was not good enough to consider using. It is just very bad at hitting a 90% right threhold that's easy to adjust. It gets 50% right, with sane posing, or 90% right, but the adjustments are rotated and IK points are stretched to narnia to achieve it, making it impossible to adjust with a final pass.

It's pretty good at whipping up boilerplate functionality. And running a lot of initial tests for you. Not to mention fighters having obscene fidelity expectations attached.

Place holder AI 3D models and most of the code to make it work sounds doable. Animations and finalized assets I'm very skeptical of AI providing value.

You should just protype it regardless. I'm vibing a 3D FG prototype myself.

replies.author: Wild-Elevator6639
replies.body: yeah I made a model with Tripo and tried to have Astra replicate the motions, but they were awful. It suggested using Deepmotion to capture the motions so I might try that

replies.author: DamnageBeats
replies.body:
There are plenty of characters on FAB you can get. Some free, some for purchase. Same with animations. I think I saw a jiu jitsu animation set. There are definitely fighting animations. 

There is also mixamo.

replies.author: Wild-Elevator6639
replies.body:
Yeah I’m looking into Maximo. I also saw some animation packs on the Unity asset store but they’re not as comprehensive as I want.

I’m currently trying to cobble together animations from different packs, but I’m worried it’ll turn out looking weird and unnatural coming from multiple sources.

comments.author: HitMePat
comments.body: You will struggle mightily trying to get even frontier models to rig 3D assets into animations that look accurate enough to be impressive or remotely realistic.   At this point Claude and Codex both still suck at rigging 3D models.  They can do simple things like running (poorly, until you correct it many many times and keep tweaking until it's somewhat good) but definitely not complex ones like a muay Thai clinch.  Yet.  Give it six more months and I'm sure they'll be great at it.

replies.author: Wild-Elevator6639
replies.body: Yeah that's pretty much been my experience. I found some decent animation packs in the Unity Asset store but they're not quite comprehensive enough. Astra suggested using AI motion capture like Deepmotion and filming myself or someone else, but I was just wondering if there were other ways to get there without having to film (if that would even work)

replies.author: HitMePat
replies.body: I've generated clips using diffusion video models of my exact character model doing simple motions like a spinning sword slash, made a short 3 second mp4, then showed Astra or Claude Fable or Claude 5.5 the clip and said "look at this example motion in this video clip frame by frame.  animate my model to do a spinning slash just like this, judge each frame and make sure it matches the example, iterate until it's as close as you can possibly get it.  Don't let any parts of the mesh clip into other parts.  Judge from every angle" and it'll spend hours and tons of tokens and still give me something that looks no where close to as good as the video clip.   And my model is already rigged really well to the skeleton.  It can't move the bones in the way the video clip shows, even when it tries really hard.

comments.author: Kasonanvu
comments.body: Make a prototype and investigate mixamo animations

comments.author: pineappleoptics
comments.body: Good luck with animations. Add in grappling and you couldn't ask for a more complicated game to make

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey! Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. Yeah, I think the overall stack is realistic, but I’d separate the problem into two parts: character creation and combat animation.

Tripo/Meshy can help get you to a base character, and Blender/Unity can handle the production side, but realistic Muay Thai is where things get harder. Clinch work, weight transfer, footwork, checks, elbows, knees, etc. need really good animation data and clean deformation.

I’d probably prototype one fighter first and prove out a few core moves before trying to build the whole roster.

Curious what you care about most right now: getting the character pipeline working, or getting the combat motion to feel believable?

replies.author: Wild-Elevator6639
replies.body:
Thanks for the response! Right now, getting the combat motion to feel believable is the priority. Tripo is pretty accurate with the character creation, though I think I’d like a little more control making adjustments. But getting realistic animations is a bitch.

I was initially trying to train Astra on YouTube videos but it was a mess
